elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause opens "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY...", replacing the one-way "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY"; no residual language leaves Client uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cap remains "TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and the 12 months run from the period generally rather than from the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages for either party; only the monetary cap was edited.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Parenthetical carves out "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION" and applies to "A PARTY'S" obligations, so it runs both ways.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No data protection or security carve-out appears in the rendered parenthetical; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are excluded.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION" places indemnities outside the cap for both parties, including the Client indemnity in Section 12a.

"A PARTY'S ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT ... NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION"; the former narrowing words "DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S" are gone, so the carve-out is now mutual and unrestricted.
Same parenthetical expressly excludes "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" of either party from the limitation.
No fraud carve-out in the rendered language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out; infringement liability outside the indemnity route would remain capped.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing states that Client's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes; the mutualised cap could be read to limit Client's fee liability.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ..." — the cap now binds Client and TrueLink symmetrically over the retained Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — a 12-month fee basis tied to the compensation for the hosting and support services that are the subject of this Agreement, not an illusory set-up-fee subset.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ... NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION".
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE ... NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION", now applicable to either party.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT ... NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION", now applicable to either party.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the cap is expressly mutual ("EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY"), the existing 12-month hosting-and-support fee basis is retained verbatim, and indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are all placed outside the limitation for both parties.

Preferred level is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", 12 months not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim, no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, nor an exclusion of Client payment obligations from capped damages.

Minimality holds: only two edits were made — the party reference was mutualised and the existing GN/WM parenthetical was expanded into the four-item carve-out list. The removed words ("DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S") sit inside the gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out element itself, and the Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope, the cap amount language and all surrounding text are untouched. No survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is left undefined (TrueLink is now covered by "either party"), no cross-reference dangles, and the retained indemnity in Section 12a is not contradicted because indemnification obligations are expressly outside the cap.

Residual note for the drafter (not a defect at fallback): if the Agreement charges compensation other than for hosting and support services, the retained cap basis captures only a subset of fees; if a subsequent round is available, replace it with "fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement" and add the USD 1,000,000 floor, the event-anchored 12-month window, a mutual consequential-damages waiver, and the data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs plus the payment-obligations exclusion to reach the preferred position.
